questions.question: Which of the following is the correct formula for ethyne?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**C2H2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ethyne**, also known as acetylene, is a hydrocarbon and the simplest alkyne with the chemical formula **C2H2**.
 
• It consists of two carbon atoms triple-bonded to each other, with each carbon also bonded to one hydrogen atom.
 
• This compound is widely used in welding and cutting due to its high flame temperature when burned with oxygen.
 
• Ethyne is a colorless gas with a slight garlic-like odor, detectable at concentrations above 100 ppm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alkynes**

 
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons with at least one carbon-carbon triple bond.
 
• The general formula for alkynes is CnH2n-2, indicating two fewer hydrogens than alkanes.
 
• They are unsaturated compounds, making them more reactive than alkanes and alkenes.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Ethyne**
 
 
• Used in oxyacetylene welding and cutting due to its high flame temperature.
 
• Serves as a precursor for synthesizing various organic chemicals.
 
• Used in the production of polymers like polyvinyl chloride (PVC).
 
 
 
• **Properties of Ethyne**
 
 
• Colorless gas with a slightly sweet odor.
 
• Highly flammable and can form explosive mixtures with air.
 
• Soluble in organic solvents like acetone and benzene.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• Store in a well-ventilated area away from sources of ignition.
 
• Use appropriate personal protective equipment when handling.
 
• Ensure proper ventilation when using in confined spaces to avoid accumulation.

questions.question: A constant force F acts on a box of mass 10 kg for a duration of 2 s. It increases the object's velocity from 6 m/s to 10 m/s. The magnitude of the applied force F is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The change in velocity (Δv) of the box is given by the difference between the final velocity and the initial velocity, which is 10 m/s - 6 m/s = 4 m/s.
 
• The time duration (t) during which the force acts is 2 seconds.
 
• Using the formula for acceleration (a) a = Δv / t, we get a = 4 m/s / 2 s = 2 m/s².
 
• According to Newton's second law of motion, Force (F) is given by F = m * a, where m is the mass of the object.
 
• Substituting the values, F = 10 kg * 2 m/s² = 20 N.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:**

 
 
• This law states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of that object times its acceleration (F = m * a).
 
• It explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration (a):**
 
 
• It is the rate of change of velocity of an object.
 
• It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction.
 
 
 
• **Force (F):**
 
 
• A push or pull acting upon an object as a result of its interaction with another object.
 
• Measured in Newtons (N) in the International System of Units (SI).
 
 
 
• **Velocity (v):**
 
 
• The speed of something in a given direction.
 
• It is also a vector quantity, meaning it includes both speed and direction.

questions.question: Which of the following is absent in cells of meristematic tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vacuoles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Meristematic tissues are composed of actively dividing cells that are responsible for the growth of plants.
 
• Cells in meristematic tissues are characterized by a prominent nucleus and dense cytoplasm.
 
• These cells have thin primary cell walls that are flexible to facilitate cell division.
 
• Vacuoles are generally absent in meristematic cells as they would hinder cell division by occupying space.
 
• The absence of vacuoles allows these cells to remain small and divide rapidly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Meristematic Tissue:**

 
 
• Meristematic tissues are classified into three types: apical, lateral, and intercalary meristems.
 
• Apical meristems are found at the tips of roots and shoots and are responsible for primary growth.
 
• Lateral meristems, such as the vascular cambium and cork cambium, contribute to the secondary growth of plants.
 
• Intercalary meristems are located at the base of leaves or internodes and help in the elongation of these parts.
 
 
 
• **Cell Division:**
 
 
• Cell division in meristematic tissues occurs through the process of mitosis, ensuring that new cells are identical to the parent cells.
 
• Mitosis involves several stages, including prophase, metaphase, anaphase, and telophase.
 
• Rapid cell division in meristematic tissues is essential for plant growth and the repair of damaged tissues.
 
 
 
• **Cell Differentiation:**
 
 
• As cells in meristematic tissues divide and mature, they undergo differentiation to form specialized tissues.
 
• Cell differentiation leads to the formation of various plant tissues such as epidermal, ground, and vascular tissues.
 
• This process is regulated by genetic and environmental factors, ensuring proper development and function of plant organs.

questions.question: ​A resistor whose value R = 10 Ω is connected to a 10-volt battery. What will be the power P and the amount of heat H generated in one minute?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Power (P) is calculated using the formula P = V²/R, where V is the voltage and R is the resistance.
 
• Given V = 10 volts and R = 10 ohms, the power P = (10)² / 10 = 10 watts.
 
• The amount of heat (H) generated is given by H = P × t, where t is the time in seconds.
 
• For one minute (60 seconds), H = 10 watts × 60 seconds = 600 joules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ohm's Law**

 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The formula is given by V = IR, where V is the voltage, I is the current, and R is the resistance.
 
 
 
• **Power in Electrical Circuits**
 
 
• Power in an electrical circuit is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit.
 
• It is calculated using P = VI, where P is power, V is voltage, and I is current.
 
• It can also be calculated using P = I²R or P = V²/R.
 
 
 
• **Heat Energy**
 
 
• Heat energy is a form of energy that is transferred between systems or objects with different temperatures.
 
• In electrical circuits, heat generated (H) can be calculated using H = P × t.
 
• The unit of heat energy is the joule (J).
 
 
 
• **SI Units**
 
 
• The International System of Units (SI) is the modern form of the metric system.
 
• Volt (V) is the unit of electric potential.
 
• Ohm (Ω) is the unit of electrical resistance.
 
• Watt (W) is the unit of power.
 
• Joule (J) is the unit of energy.

questions.question:
If the mode of the following data is 6, then find the value of k.

2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Mode** is the observation with the **highest frequency**.

Given **Mode = 6**. Frequency of 6 is 3 and frequency of 7 is 3.

To make 6 the unique mode, the term **2k + 1** must be equal to 6.

⇒ 2k + 1 = 6 ⇒ 2k = 5 ⇒ k = 2.5

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Data set: 2, 4, 6, 7, 5, 6, 10, 6, 7, 2k + 1, 9, 7, 13. Given **Mode = 6**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7325a6c1fa4f456f9c0e71986e54bca5ec81cbc8675e91fcaef38c46af87506b.png] 

Frequency distribution of known values:

⇒ Number 6 appears **3 times**.

⇒ Number 7 appears **3 times**.

⇒ Number 2 appears 1 time, 4 appears 1 time, 5 appears 1 time, 10, 9, 13 appear 1 time each.

⇒ Since the **Mode** is given as 6, its frequency must be strictly greater than any other observation.

⇒ Frequency of 6 must be 4 to exceed frequency of 7.

⇒ Therefore, the missing term 2k + 1 must be 6.

⇒ 2k + 1 = 6

⇒ 2k = 6 − 1

⇒ 2k = 5

⇒ k = 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5

**∴ The correct answer is 2.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of Mode

The mode is the value that appears most frequently in a data set. A set may be unimodal, bimodal, or multimodal.

Empirical Formula

The relationship between Mean, Median, and Mode is: Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean.

Grouped Data Mode

For grouped data, Mode = l + [(f₁ − f₀) / (2f₁ − f₀ − f₂)] × h, where l is the lower limit of the modal class.</p

questions.question: How many numbers between 11 and 90 are divisible by 7?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the first and last multiples of **7** within the range **11** to **90**.

First multiple (**a**) = **14**; Last multiple (**l**) = **84**.

Number of terms (**n**) = [(Last − First) ÷ Common Difference] + 1.

**n** = [(84 − 14) ÷ 7] + 1 = [70 ÷ 7] + 1 = 10 + 1 = **11**.

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers between **11** and **90** divisible by **7**.

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Progression (AP) nth term: **aₙ = a + (n − 1)d**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6cb6a481e49ce8621030f682261b455083c6c0937f035c5f18766f98a23b1031.png] 

⇒ First term (**a**) = 14

⇒ Common difference (**d**) = 7

⇒ Last term (**aₙ**) = 84

⇒ 84 = 14 + (n − 1) × 7

⇒ 70 = (n − 1) × 7

⇒ 10 = n − 1

⇒ n = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression (AP)

A sequence where the difference between consecutive terms is constant. Sum of **n** terms Sₙ = (n/2)[2a + (n−1)d].

Divisibility Rule of 7

Double the last digit and subtract it from the remaining number. If the result is divisible by 7, the original number is too.

Quotient Method for Range

Number of multiples of **x** up to **N** is floor(N/x). For range [A, B], count is floor(B/x) − floor((A−1)/x).</p

questions.question: Find the correct number of atoms for a glucose molecule.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**24**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A glucose molecule has the chemical formula **C6H12O6**.
 
• This formula indicates that there are **6 carbon atoms**, **12 hydrogen atoms**, and **6 oxygen atoms**.
 
• Summing up these atoms: 6 (C) + 12 (H) + 6 (O) = **24 atoms** in total.
 
• Glucose is a simple sugar and a key energy source for living organisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monosaccharides:**

 
 
• Glucose is classified as a monosaccharide, which is the simplest form of carbohydrates.
 
• Monosaccharides cannot be hydrolyzed to simpler chemical compounds.
 
• They are fundamental units of carbohydrates and are important as energy sources.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis:**
 
 
• Glucose is produced by plants during photosynthesis.
 
• It involves converting carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen using sunlight.
 
• Glucose acts as an energy storage molecule in plants.
 
 
 
• **Cellular Respiration:**
 
 
• In animals and humans, glucose is broken down during cellular respiration to release energy.
 
• It involves glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and the electron transport chain.
 
• ATP, the energy currency of the cell, is produced in this process.
 
 
 
• **Isomers of Glucose:**
 
 
• Glucose has several isomers, such as galactose and fructose.
 
• Isomers have the same molecular formula but different structural arrangements.
 
• These structural differences can significantly affect their biological roles and properties.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

(i) Suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

(ii) The particles of a suspension scatter a beam of light passing through it and make its path visible.

(iii) The solute particles settle down when a suspension is left undisturbed, that is, a suspension is unstable.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A suspension is a type of heterogeneous mixture where the solute particles do not dissolve but remain suspended throughout the medium.
 
• The particles in a suspension are large enough to scatter light, which makes the path of a light beam passing through the suspension visible (Tyndall effect).
 
• Suspensions are unstable. When left undisturbed, the particles eventually settle down due to gravity.
 
• Suspensions can be separated into their individual components through filtration, as the particles are large enough to be trapped by the filter paper.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colloids:**

 
 
• Colloids are mixtures where the particle size is intermediate between those in solutions and suspensions.
 
• The particles in a colloid do not settle down when the mixture is left undisturbed.
 
• Colloidal particles can scatter light (Tyndall effect), making the path of the light beam visible.
 
 
 
• **Solutions:**
 
 
• Solutions are homogeneous mixtures where the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent.
 
• The particles in a solution are at the molecular or ionic level and cannot be seen by the naked eye.
 
• Solutions do not scatter light and are stable, meaning the solute does not settle out over time.
 
 
 
• **Filtration:**
 
 
• Filtration is a physical separation process that separates solid particles from liquids or gases using a filter medium that allows the fluid to pass through but retains the solid particles.
 
• It is commonly used to separate suspensions into their components.
 
 
 
• **Tyndall Effect:**
 
 
• The Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by particles in a colloid or particles in a very fine suspension.
 
• This effect is used to distinguish between true solutions and colloidal solutions.

questions.question: Which of the following is INCORRECT about parenchyma?

options.text: It consists of relatively unspecialised cells with thin cell walls.
In aquatic plants, large air cavities are present in parenchyma to help them float.
It allows the bending of various parts of a plant like tendrils and stems of climbers without breaking.
The cells of parenchyma are living cells and are usually loosely arranged.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Parenchyma cells are known for their thin cell walls and relatively unspecialized functions.
 
• In aquatic plants, parenchyma cells contain large air cavities that aid in buoyancy, helping the plants float.
 
• Parenchyma cells are living cells and are usually loosely arranged, which allows for the storage of nutrients and water.
 
• Unlike collenchyma cells, parenchyma does not provide flexibility and strength to plant parts like tendrils and stems of climbers; this is a function of collenchyma cells.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Collenchyma Cells**

 
 
• Collenchyma cells have thicker cell walls compared to parenchyma and are typically found in regions of the plant that require support.
 
• These cells provide structural support and flexibility to the plant, allowing it to withstand various mechanical stresses.
 
 
 
• **Sclerenchyma Cells**
 
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are known for their extremely thick cell walls and are usually dead at maturity.
 
• These cells provide the primary structural support in plants, contributing to the hardness of seeds and nuts.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Parenchyma Cells**
 
 
• They are involved in storage, secretion, and photosynthesis in plants.
 
• Parenchyma cells also play a crucial role in the healing and repair of plant tissues.
 
 
 
• **Types of Parenchyma**
 
 
• **Chlorenchyma:** Contains chloroplasts and is involved in photosynthesis.
 
• **Aerenchyma:** Contains large air spaces to facilitate buoyancy in aquatic plants.

questions.question: In a situation where we are injured and start bleeding, the bleeding could lead to a loss of pressure that could reduce the efficiency of the pumping system. To avoid this, which cells mainly help to clot blood at the injury point?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Blood platelets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Blood platelets, or thrombocytes, are small cell fragments in the blood that are crucial for blood clotting.**
 
• They gather at the site of a blood vessel injury and form a plug by clumping together, which helps to stop bleeding.
 
• Platelets release chemicals that further help in the coagulation process by converting fibrinogen into fibrin threads, creating a stable blood clot.
 
• The normal platelet count in a healthy individual ranges from 150,000 to 450,000 platelets per microliter of blood.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coagulation Cascade:**

 
 
• The process of blood clotting is known as the coagulation cascade, involving a series of steps where various clotting factors are activated sequentially.
 
• This cascade is divided into the intrinsic, extrinsic, and common pathways, all leading to the formation of a stable blood clot.
 
 
 
• **Fibrinogen:**
 
 
• Fibrinogen is a soluble plasma protein that is converted into fibrin during blood clot formation.
 
• Fibrin strands weave through the platelet plug, solidifying the clot and preventing further bleeding.
 
 
 
• **Hemostasis:**
 
 
• Hemostasis is the process that prevents and stops bleeding, or hemorrhage.
 
• It involves vascular spasm, platelet plug formation, and blood coagulation.
 
 
 
• **Thrombocytopenia:**
 
 
• A condition characterized by abnormally low levels of platelets.
 
• It can lead to excessive bleeding and difficulty in forming blood clots.

questions.question: A cistern has two taps attached to it. Tap B can empty the cistern in 45 minutes. But Tap A can fill the cistern in just 30 minutes. Rohit started both taps unknowingly but realised his mistake after 30 minutes. He immediately closed Tap B. Now after this, in how much time will the cistern be filled?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Capacity** of the cistern = **LCM(30, 45) = 90 units**.

**Efficiency** of Tap A = 90 ÷ 30 = **+3 units/min** (Filling).

**Efficiency** of Tap B = 90 ÷ 45 = **−2 units/min** (Emptying).

Combined efficiency = 3 − 2 = **1 unit/min**. In 30 minutes, 30 units are filled.

**Remaining work** = 90 − 30 = **60 units**. Only Tap A fills it: 60 ÷ 3 = **20 min**.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 min.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Filling time of Tap A = 30 min, Emptying time of Tap B = 45 min. Both open for 30 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency.

 
 **Tap** **Time (min)** **Total Work (LCM)** **Efficiency** 
 A (Fill) 30 90 units +3 
 B (Empty) 45 −2 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Net efficiency when both are open = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/min.

⇒ Amount filled in 30 minutes = 1 × 30 = 30 units.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 90 − 30 = 60 units.

⇒ Time taken by Tap A alone to fill 60 units = Remaining Work ÷ Efficiency of A.

⇒ Time = 60 ÷ 3 = 20 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 20 min.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Efficiency

Filling pipes have **positive efficiency** while emptying pipes (leakage/taps) have **negative efficiency**.

Net Work Done

If pipe A fills in 'x' hours and pipe B empties in 'y' hours, net work in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y).

LCM Method

Always take the **LCM of time** to assume the total capacity of the tank for easier integer calculations.</p

questions.question: Which of the following pigments is present in the red blood corpuscles of human beings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Haemoglobin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Haemoglobin** is the iron-containing protein in red blood cells responsible for transporting oxygen from the lungs to the rest of the body.
 
• Each haemoglobin molecule can bind up to four oxygen molecules, enabling efficient oxygen transport.
 
• Haemoglobin also plays a critical role in transporting carbon dioxide from tissues back to the lungs for exhalation.
 
• The presence of haemoglobin gives red blood cells their characteristic red color.
 
• Normal haemoglobin levels vary by age and sex, with adult males typically having 13.8 to 17.2 grams per deciliter and females having 12.1 to 15.1 grams per deciliter.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs)**

 
 
• RBCs are the most common type of blood cell and the primary means of delivering oxygen to body tissues via blood flow.
 
• They are produced in the bone marrow and have a lifespan of about 120 days.
 
• RBCs are biconcave in shape, which increases their surface area for oxygen absorption.
 
• The average diameter of a human red blood cell is about 6-8 micrometers.
 
 
 
• **Oxygen Transport**
 
 
• Oxygen is carried in the blood bound to haemoglobin within red blood cells.
 
• Oxygen binds to the iron atoms in haemoglobin molecules in the lungs, forming oxyhaemoglobin.
 
• This oxygen is then released to tissues throughout the body where it is needed for cellular respiration.
 
 
 
• **Carbon Dioxide Transport**
 
 
• Carbon dioxide produced as a waste product of cellular respiration is transported back to the lungs in several forms.
 
• About 20-25% of CO2 is carried by haemoglobin as carbaminohaemoglobin.
 
• The majority of CO2 is converted to bicarbonate ions (HCO3-) in the blood plasma.
 
• In the lungs, CO2 is released from haemoglobin and exhaled out of the body.
 
 
 
• **Iron in Haemoglobin**
 
 
• Iron is a critical component of haemoglobin and is necessary for its oxygen-carrying capacity.
 
• Each haemoglobin molecule contains four iron atoms, each capable of binding one oxygen molecule.
 
• Iron deficiency can lead to anaemia, a condition characterized by reduced oxygen-carrying capacity of the blood.

**Calculations:**

⇒ a = (6 × 2) / √3
 
⇒ a = 12 / √3 = 4√3 cm
 
⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × (4√3)²
 
⇒ Area = (√3 / 4) × (16 × 3)
 
⇒ Area = √3 × 4 × 3
 
⇒ Area = 12√3 cm²

Equilateral Triangle Properties

Inradius and Circumradius
 
**Inradius (r)** = a / (2√3) and **Circumradius (R)** = a / √3, where 'a' is the side length.
 
Perimeter
 
The **perimeter** of an equilateral triangle is 3 × side (3a).</p

sin θ × cosec θ = 1, cos θ × sec θ = 1, and tan θ × cot θ = 1.</p

questions.question: The sum of the two numbers is 58 and one of them exceeds the other by 18. Find the greater number.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For two numbers, if **Sum (S)** and **Difference (D)** are given:

**Greater Number** = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2

⇒ (58 + 18) ÷ 2

⇒ 76 ÷ 2 = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Sum of two numbers = 58

Difference between numbers = 18

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2354b9bda62a0a80bfd4fc881cc474833c2b6508fe646536d8bbd6a46c2cfc55.png]

⇒ x − y = 18 --- (ii)

Adding equation (i) and (ii):

⇒ (x + y) + (x − y) = 58 + 18

⇒ 2x = 76

⇒ x = 76 ÷ 2

⇒ x = 38

**∴ The correct answer is 38.**

**__Additional Information__**

Finding the Smaller Number

The smaller number can be found using the formula (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 or by subtracting the difference from the greater number.

Linear Equations in Two Variables

When solving x + y = A and x − y = B, the values are always x = (A+B)/2 and y = (A−B)/2.</p

questions.question: Which hormone helps in development of the female sex organs and regulates the menstrual cycle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oestrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Oestrogen** is primarily responsible for the development and regulation of the female reproductive system and secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• This hormone plays a crucial role in the development of the breasts, endometrium, regulation of the menstrual cycle, and reproductive system maintenance.
 
• Oestrogen levels fluctuate during the menstrual cycle, peaking during the ovulatory phase to prepare the uterus for potential pregnancy.
 
• It also has significant effects on other tissues, including bone, liver, and the cardiovascular system, contributing to overall female health.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Oestrogen levels are highest during the follicular and ovulatory phases, facilitating ovulation and preparation of the uterine lining for implantation.
 
 
 
• **Progesterone**
 
 
• Another critical hormone in female reproductive health, it works alongside oestrogen to regulate the menstrual cycle and maintain pregnancy.
 
• Progesterone levels rise during the luteal phase after ovulation, preparing the uterus for a potential pregnancy.
 
 
 
• **Hormonal Imbalances**
 
 
• Imbalances in oestrogen levels can lead to conditions such as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, and other menstrual disorders.
 
• Treatment for hormonal imbalances may include lifestyle changes, medications, and sometimes hormone replacement therapy.
 
 
 
• **Role in Bone Health**
 
 
• Oestrogen helps maintain bone density by inhibiting bone resorption, reducing the risk of osteoporosis post-menopause.
 
• Women are more susceptible to osteoporosis due to the drop in oestrogen levels after menopause.

questions.question: Which statement is correct for unsaturated hydrocarbons?

options.text: Methane, ethane and butane are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Cyclo pentane and hexane are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Alkane, alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.
Alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alkenes and alkynes are unsaturated hydrocarbons.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Unsaturated hydrocarbons** are organic compounds that contain double or triple bonds between carbon atoms.
 
• **Alkenes** are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon double bond (C=C).
 
• **Alkynes** are hydrocarbons that contain at least one carbon-carbon triple bond (C≡C).
 
• Examples of alkenes include **ethylene (C2H4)** and propylene (C3H6).
 
• Examples of alkynes include **acetylene (C2H2)** and propyne (C3H4).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** (alkanes) only contain single bonds between carbon atoms and are fully saturated with hydrogen atoms.
 
• Alkenes and alkynes are more reactive than alkanes due to the presence of double and triple bonds, which have higher energy and are more chemically reactive.
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons can undergo addition reactions, where atoms or groups of atoms are added to the carbon atoms involved in the double or triple bonds.
 
• **Hydrogenation** is a chemical process where unsaturated hydrocarbons are converted to saturated hydrocarbons by adding hydrogen (H2).
 
• Unsaturated hydrocarbons play a crucial role in the chemical industry, including the production of polymers, pharmaceuticals, and other organic compounds.

questions.question: What sum will earn a simple interest of ₹1,056 in 3 years at 16% per year rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective **Rate of Interest** = 16% × 3 = 48%

Given, 48% of **Principal** = ₹1,056

**Principal** (100%) = (1056 ÷ 48) × 100 = 22 × 100

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Simple Interest** (SI) = ₹1,056

**Time** (T) = 3 years

**Rate** (R) = 16% per annum

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2cc76775864b7c74816723027fef21834f1c42be8fe124bc7ca6212ea96f45db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1056 = (P × 16 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 1056 = (P × 48) ÷ 100

⇒ P = (1056 × 100) ÷ 48

⇒ P = 22 × 100

⇒ P = 2200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,200.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The total **Amount** (A) at the end of the period is the sum of **Principal** and **Interest**: A = P + SI = P[1 + (RT/100)].

Rule of Simple Interest

In **Simple Interest**, the interest remains constant for every year because it is always calculated on the original **Principal**.

Effective Rate Method

Effective Rate = R × T. This helps in directly calculating the **Interest** or **Principal** using percentage comparison.

questions.question: If future shoot hidden in a germinating seed is called plumule, then future root of the germinating seed would be _______.

__
 
• The radicle is the part of a plant embryo that develops into the primary root.
 
• It is the first part of the seedling to emerge from the seed during the process of germination.
 
• The radicle grows downward into the soil, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients.
 
• This structure is crucial for the seedling’s early growth and establishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plumule:**

 
 
• The plumule is the part of the seed embryo that develops into the shoot bearing the first true leaves of a plant.
 
• It grows upward, emerging from the soil, and facilitates photosynthesis for the young plant.
 
 
 
• **Cotyledon:**
 
 
• Cotyledons are the first leaves that appear from a germinating seed.
 
• They are sometimes referred to as seed leaves and can store food for the seedling.
 
 
 
• **Seed Germination:**
 
 
• Germination is the process by which a seed develops into a new plant.
 
• It typically involves imbibition (water absorption), enzyme activation, and the growth of the radicle and plumule.
 
 
 
• **Embryo Structure:**
 
 
• The seed embryo consists of the radicle, plumule, and cotyledons.
 
• These structures are critical for the initial growth and development of the plant.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement related to tropism.

options.text: Geotropism - in response to the pull of earth or gravity

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phototropism - movement towards water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Phototropism** is the growth movement of a plant in response to light. Plants typically grow towards the light source, which is known as positive phototropism.
 
• It is primarily regulated by the plant hormone auxin, which redistributes towards the shaded side of the plant, causing cell elongation and bending towards the light.
 
• Phototropism helps plants maximize light absorption for photosynthesis, which is essential for their growth and energy production.
 
• Unlike hydrotropism, which involves movement towards water, phototropism involves movement towards a light source. Therefore, the statement "Phototropism - movement towards water" is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydrotropism**

 
 
• Hydrotropism is the growth response of plant roots towards water. This allows the plant to maximize water uptake, which is crucial for various physiological processes.
 
• Unlike phototropism, which is influenced by light, hydrotropism is influenced by moisture gradients in the soil.
 
 
 
• **Geotropism**
 
 
• Geotropism, also known as gravitropism, is the growth response of plants to gravity. Roots typically exhibit positive geotropism (growing downwards), while stems show negative geotropism (growing upwards).
 
• This response ensures that roots anchor the plant and access water and nutrients, while stems grow towards the light.
 
 
 
• **Thigmotropism**
 
 
• Thigmotropism is the directional growth response of plants to touch or physical contact. It is commonly observed in climbing plants and vines.
 
• Examples include tendrils of pea plants wrapping around a support structure.
 
 
 
• **Chemotropism**
 
 
• Chemotropism is the growth response of a plant to a chemical stimulus. For example, the growth of pollen tubes towards ovules during fertilization is driven by chemotropic signals.
 
• This type of tropism ensures that fertilization occurs successfully within flowering plants.

questions.question: Which gas is given out when metals react with dilute hydrochloric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hydrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When metals react with dilute hydrochloric acid, they typically release **hydrogen gas**.
 
• The reaction can be generalized as: Metal + Dilute Hydrochloric Acid → Metal Chloride + Hydrogen Gas.
 
• For example, when zinc reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid, zinc chloride and hydrogen gas are formed: Zn + 2HCl → ZnCl₂ + H₂.
 
• Hydrogen gas is typically observed as bubbles forming on the surface of the metal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series of Metals**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a ranking of metals based on their reactivity with acids and water.
 
• Metals higher in the series, such as potassium and sodium, react more vigorously with acids compared to metals lower in the series, such as gold and platinum.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Hydrogen Gas**
 
 
• Hydrogen is a colorless, odorless, and highly flammable gas.
 
• It is the lightest element and is used in various industrial applications, including hydrogen fuel cells.
 
 
 
• **Safety Precautions**
 
 
• When conducting reactions that produce hydrogen gas, proper ventilation and safety measures should be in place to prevent accumulation and potential explosions.
 
• Hydrogen gas should be handled with care due to its flammability.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Hydrogen**
 
 
• Hydrogen is used in the production of ammonia for fertilizers, in refining metals, and as a fuel in hydrogen fuel cells.
 
• It is also used in the food industry for hydrogenation of fats and oils.

questions.question: An electric bulb is connected to a 200 V generator. The current drawn by the bulb is 0.1 A. What is the power of the bulb?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 W**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The power (P) consumed by an electrical device can be calculated using the formula **P = V × I**, where V is the voltage and I is the current.
 
• In this case, the electric bulb is connected to a 200 V generator and it draws a current of 0.1 A.
 
• By substituting the given values into the formula: **P = 200 V × 0.1 A = 20 W**.
 
• Therefore, the power consumed by the bulb is **20 W**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Power (P)**

 
 
• Power is the rate at which electrical energy is consumed or converted into another form (like light, heat, etc.).
 
• It is measured in watts (W).
 
 
 
• **Voltage (V)**
 
 
• Voltage is the electric potential difference between two points and is measured in volts (V).
 
• It drives the current through a circuit.
 
 
 
• **Current (I)**
 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge and is measured in amperes (A).
 
• It is the rate at which charge passes through a point in a circuit.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law**
 
 
• Ohm's Law states that the current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
 
• The mathematical expression is **V = I × R**, where R is the resistance.

questions.question: In its October 2024 meeting, the RBI Monetary Policy Meeting kept the _____ unchanged at 6.5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• As of October 2024, the RBI kept the repo rate unchanged at 6.5% during its Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting.
 
• Maintaining the repo rate can influence interest rates in the economy, impacting both inflation and economic growth.
 
• The decision to keep the repo rate unchanged is often based on current economic indicators such as inflation rates, GDP growth, and other macroeconomic factors.
 
• Repo rate adjustments are a key tool used by the RBI to maintain liquidity and control inflation in the economy.

• CRR is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the RBI in the form of reserves.
 
• It ensures that banks do not run out of cash to meet the payment demands of their depositors.
 
 
 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**
 
 
• SLR is the minimum percentage of deposits that a commercial bank has to maintain in the form of liquid cash, gold, or other securities.
 
• This is a tool used by the RBI to control the expansion of credit.
 
 
 
• **Bank Rate**
 
 
• The bank rate is the rate at which the central bank of a country lends money to domestic banks, often for long-term purposes.
 
• Changes in the bank rate can impact the overall lending rates in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**
 
 
• The MPC is a committee of the RBI responsible for formulating the monetary policy of India.
 
• It consists of six members, including the RBI Governor as the chairperson.
 
• The MPC meets bi-monthly to review and decide on key policy rates, including the repo rate.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Control**
 
 
• Inflation control is one of the primary objectives of the RBI's monetary policy.
 
• By adjusting the repo rate, the RBI aims to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

questions.question: Decomposition of limestone to quick lime and carbon dioxide is an example of which of the following types of reaction?

__
 
• Decomposition of limestone (CaCO₃) to quick lime (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) occurs when heated strongly.
 
• This process is known as thermal decomposition, which involves breaking down a compound by heating.
 
• Thermal decomposition reactions require energy in the form of heat to break chemical bonds in the reactant.
 
• In the case of limestone, the reaction can be represented as: CaCO₃ (s) → CaO (s) + CO₂ (g).
 
• Thermal decomposition is commonly used in various industrial processes, including the production of cement and lime.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photochemical decomposition**

 
 
• It involves the breaking down of a compound by the action of light, typically ultraviolet light.
 
• Example: Decomposition of silver chloride (AgCl) into silver (Ag) and chlorine (Cl₂) under sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Reduction reaction**
 
 
• A chemical reaction that involves the gain of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• Reduction is typically accompanied by oxidation, which involves the loss of electrons.
 
 
 
• **Oxidation reaction**
 
 
• A chemical reaction that involves the loss of electrons by a molecule, atom, or ion.
 
• Oxidation reactions are often paired with reduction reactions in redox processes.
 
 
 
• **Industrial uses of quick lime**
 
 
• Quick lime (CaO) is used in the manufacture of cement and concrete.
 
• It is also used for soil stabilization, water treatment, and as a flux in steelmaking.

questions.question: Manish bought an electronic gadget with a 25% discount on the MRP. He made a profit of ₹600 by selling it for Rs. 18,600. The marked price of the electronic gadget was:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 18,600 and Profit = Rs. 600.

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit = 18,600 − 600 = Rs. 18,000.

Discount = 25%, so CP is 75% of the Marked Price (MRP).

75% of MRP = 18,000 ⇒ 3/4 × MRP = 18,000.

MRP = 18,000 × 4 ÷ 3 = 6,000 × 4 = Rs. 24,000.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 24,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP = Rs. 18,600, Profit = Rs. 600, Discount % = 25%.

**Formulas:** CP = SP − Profit | MRP = CP ÷ (1 − Discount%/100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a294aef385ea764d445ecbabaf1d9104bd4a987ddb639f5392b8ff78dffd8628.png] 

⇒ **Cost Price (CP)** of the gadget = Selling Price − Profit

⇒ CP = 18,600 − 600 = 18,000

⇒ Let **Marked Price (MRP)** be x.

⇒ Discounted price = x − 25% of x = 0.75x

questions.question: Which metals produce hydrogen gas when treated with very dilute nitric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium (Mg) and manganese (Mn)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Magnesium (Mg)** and **manganese (Mn)** react with very dilute nitric acid to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• When **Mg and Mn** are treated with dilute nitric acid, they displace hydrogen from the acid to form magnesium nitrate and manganese nitrate, respectively, while releasing hydrogen gas.
 
• Other metals like **copper (Cu)** and **cobalt (Co)** do not react with dilute nitric acid to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• The production of hydrogen gas depends on the reactivity series of metals where **Mg and Mn** are more reactive compared to metals like copper.

• **Reactivity Series**

 
 
• A ranking of metals based on their reactivity with water, acids, and oxygen.
 
• Highly reactive metals like potassium and sodium can react vigorously with water.
 
• Moderately reactive metals like magnesium and manganese react with acids to release hydrogen gas.
 
• Less reactive metals like copper and gold do not react with dilute acids to release hydrogen gas.
 
 
 
• **Nitric Acid (HNO3)**
 
 
• A strong acid commonly used in laboratories and industries.
 
• Concentrated nitric acid is a strong oxidizing agent and can react violently with metals.
 
• Very dilute nitric acid, however, behaves differently and can produce hydrogen gas with some reactive metals.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Gas (H2)**

• Produced in reactions involving acids and reactive metals.
 
• It is used in various industrial processes including hydrogenation and as a fuel in some applications.

questions.question: What determines the colour of scattered light in the Tyndall effect?

options.text: The size of the scattering particles.
The angle of incidence of the incoming light.
The distance between the source of light and the scattering particles.
The angle of refraction of the emerging light.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The size of the scattering particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Tyndall effect occurs when light is scattered by particles in its path.
 
• The color of the scattered light depends on the size of the scattering particles.
 
• Smaller particles scatter shorter wavelengths of light (blue and violet) more effectively.
 
• Larger particles scatter longer wavelengths of light (red and orange).
 
• This is why the sky appears blue during the day and can turn red or orange during sunrise and sunset.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tyndall Effect:**

 
 
• It is the scattering of light by particles in a colloid or in very fine particles in a suspension.
 
• This effect is named after the 19th-century scientist John Tyndall, who first studied the phenomenon.
 
 
 
• **Rayleigh Scattering:**
 
 
• A special case of the Tyndall effect where the scattering particles are much smaller than the wavelength of light.
 
• This explains why the sky appears blue, as shorter wavelengths are scattered more.
 
 
 
• **Mie Scattering:**
 
 
• Occurs when the particles are larger than the wavelength of light.
 
• It is responsible for the white appearance of clouds, as all wavelengths are scattered equally.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Tyndall Effect:**
 
 
• Used in the study of colloids to determine the size and distribution of particles.
 
• Helps in the design of optical instruments and in the field of atmospheric science.

questions.question: Face cream belongs to which type of colloid form?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Emulsion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Face cream is an example of an emulsion**, which is a type of colloid where both the dispersed phase and the dispersion medium are liquids.
 
• An emulsion is formed when two immiscible liquids are mixed together, typically oil and water, with one being dispersed in the form of tiny droplets throughout the other.
 
• In face creams, the oil phase is usually dispersed within the water phase, creating an oil-in-water (O/W) emulsion.
 
• Emulsifiers are added to face creams to stabilize the emulsion, preventing the oil and water from separating.
 
• Common ingredients in face creams that act as emulsifiers include cetyl alcohol, stearic acid, and polysorbates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of Emulsions**

 
 
• **Oil-in-Water (O/W) Emulsion:** Oil droplets are dispersed in water, commonly used in cosmetic creams and lotions.
 
• **Water-in-Oil (W/O) Emulsion:** Water droplets are dispersed in oil, typically used in heavy creams and ointments.
 
 
 
• **Emulsifiers**
 
 
• Emulsifiers are substances that stabilize emulsions by reducing surface tension at the interface of the two immiscible liquids.
 
• They can be natural, like lecithin, or synthetic, like polysorbates.
 
 
 
• **Colloid**
 
 
• A colloid is a mixture where one substance is dispersed evenly throughout another at a microscopic level.
 
• Examples include gels, foams, sols, and emulsions.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Emulsions**
 
 
• Emulsions are typically opaque or translucent.
 
• They can be broken down by heating, freezing, or adding an electrolyte.

__
 
• **Reduction involves the gain of electrons**, which often corresponds to the gain of hydrogen or the loss of oxygen in a chemical reaction.
 
• **Loss of oxygen** is a key indicator of a reduction reaction.
 
• **Gain of hydrogen** is another common characteristic of reduction.
 
• Oxidation and reduction reactions always occur simultaneously in what are known as **redox reactions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oxidation**

 
 
• Oxidation is the process where an atom, ion, or molecule loses electrons.
 
• It is often accompanied by the gain of oxygen or the loss of hydrogen.
 
• Oxidation reactions release energy and are exothermic.
 
 
 
• **Redox Reactions**
 
 
• Redox reactions involve the simultaneous processes of reduction and oxidation.
 
• These reactions are vital for energy production in biological systems, such as cellular respiration.
 
 
 
• **Electrochemical Cells**
 
 
• In electrochemical cells, oxidation occurs at the anode, and reduction occurs at the cathode.
 
• These cells convert chemical energy into electrical energy or vice versa.
 
 
 
• **Importance in Industry**
 
 
• Reduction processes are crucial in metallurgy for extracting metals from their ores.
 
• They are also used in various chemical manufacturing processes.

questions.question:
A spherical mirror diverges a beam of light, which is incident on it. Which of the following statement(s) about the mirror is/are true?

i)The mirror used is convex.

ii) The mirror has positive focal length.

iii) The image formed by this mirror can be seen on a screen.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A spherical mirror that diverges a beam of light is known as a convex mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors have a positive focal length, which means the focal point is behind the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors form virtual images, which cannot be projected on a screen.
 
• These mirrors are commonly used in applications where a wide field of view is needed, such as in vehicle rearview mirrors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Convex Mirror**

 
 
• A convex mirror is a spherical mirror where the reflective surface bulges outward.
 
• They are also known as diverging mirrors because they spread out light rays that have been reflected.
 
• Convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished images.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• Focal length is the distance between the mirror's surface and the focal point.
 
• For convex mirrors, the focal length is positive.
 
• The focal point is the point where parallel light rays either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting off the mirror.
 
 
 
• **Virtual Image**
 
 
• A virtual image is an image that cannot be obtained on a screen.
 
• Virtual images are formed when light rays appear to meet at a point behind the mirror.
 
• Convex mirrors always produce virtual images.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Convex Mirrors**
 
 
• Used in vehicle rearview mirrors to provide a wider field of view.
 
• Installed in hallways and stores for security purposes to monitor a larger area.
 
• Utilized in optical instruments like telescopes to direct light.

• Incandescence is the emission of light from a hot object due to its temperature.

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 7: 5. If their sum is 360, then the difference between them will be:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
**Sum of ratio parts** = 7 + 5 = 12 units.

**Difference of ratio parts** = 7 − 5 = 2 units.

Given: 12 units = 360 → 1 unit = 30.

**Difference** = 2 units × 30 = 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of numbers = 7 : 5, Sum = 360.

**Formula:** Value = (Specific Ratio ÷ Sum of Ratios) × Total Sum
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0b2fc6f4be1e5b636ca2daa92d57824c3b66abe463d6b6d9f34764a68cd51c4c.png] 
⇒ Let the numbers be **7x** and **5x**.

⇒ Sum = 7x + 5x = 12x

⇒ 12x = 360

⇒ x = 360 ÷ 12 = 30

⇒ First number = 7 × 30 = 210

⇒ Second number = 5 × 30 = 150

⇒ Difference = 210 − 150 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio and Proportion

A **ratio** compares values. If a : b is given and the sum is S, the individual values are [a/(a+b)] × S and [b/(a+b)] × S.

Difference in Ratios

The **difference between two quantities** in a ratio a : b can be found directly as |a − b| × (Sum / (a + b)).

Compound Ratio

The **compound ratio** of a : b and c : d is (a × c) : (b × d).</p

questions.question: Vandita scored an overall average of 80% marks in five subjects taken together, viz. Hindi, Science, Maths, English and Sanskrit, wherein the maximum marks of each subject were 105. How many marks did Vandita score in Science if she scored 89 marks in Hindi, 92 marks in Sanskrit, 98 marks in Maths and 81 marks in English?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total subjects = 5, Maximum marks per subject = 105.

Average marks required = 80% of 105 = 84 per subject.

Total target deviation from 84 = 0.

Deviations: Hindi (89−84) = +5, Sanskrit (92−84) = +8, Maths (98−84) = +14, English (81−84) = −3.

Sum of deviations = 5 + 8 + 14 − 3 = +24. Science must be 84 − 24 = 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60 marks.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d85bd9a3f7b29d3e5b4723d4af9b1cfad69ee73a94276a91be9200de95a7b55.png] 

**Given:** Number of subjects = 5, Maximum marks per subject = 105.

**Formula:** Total Marks Scored = Average % × Total Maximum Marks

⇒ Total maximum marks = 5 × 105 = 525

⇒ Total marks scored by **Vandita** = 80% of 525 = 0.80 × 525 = 420

⇒ Marks in **Hindi** + **Sanskrit** + **Maths** + **English** = 89 + 92 + 98 + 81 = 360

⇒ Marks in **Science** = Total marks − Sum of other 4 subjects

⇒ Marks in **Science** = 420 − 360 = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 marks.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When different subjects have different maximum marks, the overall percentage is calculated as (Sum of marks obtained ÷ Sum of maximum marks) × 100.

Percentage to Marks Conversion

To find the absolute score from a percentage, use: Marks = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Maximum Marks.

Net Deviation Method

In any set of observations, the sum of deviations of all values from the actual mean (average) is always zero.</p

questions.question: Which of the following substances experiences the least change in shape when subjected to a change in pressure?

• Solids have a definite shape and volume, and their particles are closely packed in a fixed arrangement.
 
• Due to the strong intermolecular forces between particles, solids are highly resistant to deformation under pressure.

• Compared to liquids, gases, and plasma, solids maintain their structure and exhibit the least compressibility.

• **Gases**
 
 
• Gases have neither a definite shape nor a definite volume and expand to fill their container.
 
• The particles in gases are far apart and move freely, resulting in high compressibility.
 
• Gases experience significant changes in shape and volume under pressure.
 
 
 
• **Plasma**
 
 
• Plasma is an ionized state of matter consisting of free electrons and ions.
 
• It has properties distinct from solids, liquids, and gases, including high electrical conductivity.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about transport in plants?

options.text: The phloem moves water and minerals obtained from the soil.
In herbs and shrubs, the distances over which transport systems have to operate are very large.
The xylem transports products of photosynthesis from the leaves where they are synthesised to other parts of the plant.
Plants have low energy needs and use relatively slow transport systems.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Plants have low energy needs and use relatively slow transport systems.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plants, being autotrophic organisms, produce their own food via photosynthesis, which significantly reduces their overall energy needs compared to animals.
 
• The transport of water, minerals, and nutrients in plants occurs through xylem and phloem, which are relatively slow compared to the circulatory systems in animals.
 
• Plants rely on processes such as diffusion, osmosis, and active transport to move substances, which do not require high energy expenditure.
 
• Due to the stationary nature of plants and their low metabolic rates, the slow transport system suffices to meet their needs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Xylem**

 
 
• Xylem is responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of vessels and tracheids, which are long, tube-like structures that facilitate the movement of water.
 
• The process of water movement in xylem is driven by transpiration pull, root pressure, and capillary action.
 
 
 
• **Phloem**
 
 
• Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• It consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
 
• The movement in phloem is bidirectional, allowing nutrients to be transported to growing regions and storage tissues.
 
 
 
• **Transpiration**
 
 
• Transpiration is the process by which water vapor is lost from the aerial parts of plants, primarily through stomata.
 
• This process creates a negative pressure in the leaf, which helps in pulling water up through the xylem from the roots.
 
 
 
• **Photosynthesis**
 
 
• Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use sunlight to synthesize nutrients from carbon dioxide and water.
 
• It primarily occurs in the chloroplasts of plant cells and produces glucose and oxygen as by-products.
 
• The products of photosynthesis are transported through the phloem to various parts of the plant for growth and storage.

questions.question: A pair of parallel lines is intersected by a transversal such that ∠1 and ∠2 form a pair of alternate interior angles. If m∠1 = 75°, what is the measure of m∠2?

When a pair of **parallel lines** is intersected by a **transversal**, the **alternate interior angles** are always equal.

Given: m∠1 = 75°

Since ∠1 and ∠2 are a pair of alternate interior angles, m∠2 = m∠1.

⇒ m∠2 = 75°

Lines **L₁** and **L₂** are parallel (L₁ || L₂).

Transversal **T** intersects these lines.

Measure of angle 1 (m∠1) = 75°

∠1 and ∠2 are **alternate interior angles**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c342f6668fdc69671ac12c5cc4e247e4bd8d9c3ccdae2b3fd34af73b68f6d929.png] 

**Property Used:**

If two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the **Alternate Interior Angles Theorem** states that the resulting alternate interior angles are congruent (equal in measure).

**Calculations:**

⇒ m∠1 = m∠2 (By Alternate Interior Angles Theorem)

⇒ 75° = m∠2

⇒ m∠2 = 75°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Corresponding Angles

Angles in the same relative position at each intersection where a straight line crosses two others. For parallel lines, these are always **equal**.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Pairs of angles on one side of the transversal and between the two parallel lines. They are **supplementary**, meaning their sum is **180°**.

Alternate Exterior Angles

Pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and outside the two parallel lines. For parallel lines, these are also **equal**.</p

For **half-yearly compounding**, Rate (R) becomes R/2 and Time (n) becomes 2n.

Effective Rate = 8% ÷ 2 = 4% per half-year.

Time periods = 1 year × 2 = 2 periods.

Effective % for 2 periods = 4 + 4 + (4 × 4)/100 = 8.16%.

Amount = 7500 × 108.16% = 75 × 108.16 = ₹8112.

questions.question: The HCF of 2410 and 2700 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **common factor** by observing the last digits of both numbers.

Both **2410** and **2700** end in 0, meaning they are both divisible by **10**.

Difference between 2700 and 2410 = **290**. The HCF must be a factor of 290.

Check options: 10 is the largest factor of 290 that divides both 2410 and 2700.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are **2410** and **2700**.

**Method:** Prime Factorization Method.

⇒ 2410 = 2 × 5 × 241

⇒ 2700 = 2² × 3³ × 5² = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5

⇒ Common prime factors are **2** and **5**.

⇒ HCF = Product of common prime factors with the lowest power.

⇒ HCF = 2¹ × 5¹ = 10.

**∴ The correct answer is 10.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. Also known as **GCD (Greatest Common Divisor)**.

Division Method for HCF

Divide the larger number by the smaller number, then divide the previous divisor by the remainder until the remainder becomes zero. The last divisor is the **HCF**.

HCF and LCM Relation

For two numbers a and b: **Product of Numbers (a × b) = HCF × LCM**.</p

questions.question: Rays of the Sun converge at a point of 30 cm in front of a concave mirror. Where should the object be placed so that the size of the image is equal to the size of the object?

options.text: Between 30 and 60 cm in front of the mirror
More than 30 cm in front of the mirror
30 cm in front of the mirror
60 cm in front of the mirror

questions.solution:
The object should be placed at a distance of __**60 cm in front of the concave mirror.**__

When rays of light from a distant source like the Sun fall on a concave mirror, they are considered parallel and converge at the **principal focus (F)** of the mirror.

The problem states the rays converge at a point **30 cm** in front of the mirror. Therefore, the **focal length (F)** of the mirror is 30 cm.

For a concave mirror, the image size is **equal** to the object size only when the object is placed at the **Centre of Curvature (C)**

The relationship between the Centre of Curvature and the Focal Length is C = 2f, So C = 2 * 30 = 60 cm.Thus, the object must be placed at the Centre of Curvature, which is 60 cm in front of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **angle of incidence** is the angle between the incident ray and the normal to the surface at the point of incidence.
 
• The **angle of refraction** is the angle between the refracted ray and the normal to the surface at the point of refraction.
 
• According to **Snell's Law**, the angle of incidence is not equal to the angle of refraction except in the special case where the two media have the same refractive index.
 
• The refractive index of a medium dictates how much light bends when entering the medium from another medium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snell's Law**

 
 
• It states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence to the sine of the angle of refraction is constant for a given pair of media.
 
• This constant is known as the refractive index.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index**
 
 
• It is a measure of how much the speed of light or other waves is reduced inside a medium compared to a vacuum.
 
• It is given by the formula n = c/v, where c is the speed of light in vacuum and v is the speed of light in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Critical Angle**
 
 
• The critical angle is the angle of incidence above which total internal reflection occurs.
 
• It occurs when light tries to move from a denser medium to a less dense medium.
 
 
 
• **Total Internal Reflection**
 
 
• This phenomenon occurs when the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle.
 
• In such cases, the light is completely reflected back into the denser medium.

questions.question: The mean and mode of a set of data are 58.7 and 61.1, respectively. Find the median of the data, using the empirical formula.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **empirical relationship** between central tendencies is: 3 × **Median** = **Mode** + 2 × **Mean**

3 × Median = 61.1 + 2 × 58.7

3 × Median = 61.1 + 117.4 = 178.5

Median = 178.5 ÷ 3 = 59.5

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Mean** of the data = 58.7

**Mode** of the data = 61.1

**Formula Used:**

Mode = 3 × Median − 2 × Mean

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/677f028b625b7155f9508dc8035e0d044f1b0e6636299c6ff6d900bbf5d3c00a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 61.1 = 3 × Median − 2 × 58.7

⇒ 61.1 = 3 × Median − 117.4

⇒ 3 × Median = 61.1 + 117.4

⇒ 3 × Median = 178.5

⇒ Median = 178.5 ÷ 3

⇒ Median = 59.5

**∴ The correct answer is 59.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Distribution

In a perfectly **symmetrical distribution**, the Mean, Median, and Mode are all equal (Mean = Median = Mode).

Positive Skewness

In a **positively skewed** distribution, the values generally follow the order: Mean > Median > Mode.

Negative Skewness

In a **negatively skewed** distribution, the values generally follow the order: Mode > Median > Mean.

Empirical Rule Scope

The relationship **Mode = 3 Median − 2 Mean** is an approximation used for moderately skewed unimodal distributions.</p

questions.question: Which of the following would help a few variants of bacteria in a population living in temperate waters to survive and grow further, if the water temperature were to be increased by global warming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistant to heat**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bacteria that are resistant to heat are better equipped to survive higher temperatures.
 
• Global warming leads to an increase in average water temperatures, making heat resistance crucial for survival.
 
• Heat-resistant bacteria can continue to grow and reproduce in warmer waters, ensuring their population's continuation.
 
• These bacteria have mechanisms such as heat-shock proteins that help them withstand and adapt to elevated temperatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heat-Shock Proteins (HSPs)**

 
 
• These proteins act as molecular chaperones, helping other proteins maintain their structure and function under heat stress.
 
• HSPs are produced in larger quantities when cells are exposed to higher temperatures.
 
 
 
• **Thermophiles**
 
 
• These are microorganisms that thrive at relatively high temperatures, between 41 and 122 degrees Celsius.
 
• They are often found in hot springs and deep-sea hydrothermal vents.
 
 
 
• **Global Warming Impact on Marine Life**
 
 
• Increased water temperatures can lead to shifts in marine biodiversity.
 
• Species that cannot adapt to the new conditions may face extinction, while heat-resistant species may proliferate.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation Mechanisms**
 
 
• Bacteria adapt to environmental changes through genetic mutations and natural selection.
 
• Heat resistance may develop over generations as bacteria with heat-resistant traits survive and reproduce.
